query: For high-value components operating in aggressive environments, what intervention could improve surface physical and mechanical characteristics? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should remain effective, prior evidence that would support it, and an experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Annealing the as-deposited, strongly amorphous AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy (HEA) film at 800 °C for 1 hour in air generates a dense, protective composite oxide (primarily ZrTiO4) on the surface that improves its physical and mechanical characteristics.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, strongly amorphous AlCrTiZrMo HEA film without any post-deposition heat treatment.
generation.intervention: Annealing treatment at 800 °C for 1 hour in ambient air.
generation.conditions: The heat treatment is carried out under atmospheric conditions with subsequent evaluation performed in a tribocorrosion test setup (e.g., linear reciprocating friction test with a specified load and sliding conditions) in an oxidizing environment.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the film surface.
generation.mechanism: At 800 °C, the controlled thermal oxidation promotes the development of a compact composite oxide layer that passivates the surface. This layer minimizes further oxidation, reduces wear by increasing surface hardness, and provides tribocorrosion resistance in aggressive environments.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the untreated (as-deposited) film baseline, the annealed film will exhibit improved tribocorrosion resistance, as evidenced by a lower coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate, along with enhanced surface hardness and a denser microstructure.
generation.baseline: The as-deposited AlCrTiZrMo HEA film without the annealing treatment.
generation.boundary: The enhanced properties should remain effective during high-temperature, oxidizing, and mechanically aggressive conditions typical of critical component service environments.
generation.uncertainty: While the direction of improvement is supported, the exact magnitude of enhancement (e.g., percentage reduction in wear rate or friction) requires further quantification.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCrTiZrMo HEA films: one set will remain in the as-deposited state (control) and the other will be annealed at 800 °C for 1 hour in air. Subject both sets to identical tribocorrosion tests using a linear reciprocating friction machine (with controlled load, sliding frequency, and duration) in an oxidizing environment.
measurements: Wear rate determined from wear volume measurements
Surface morphology and microstructure via SEM and XRD to confirm oxide layer formation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed films do not show statistically significant reductions in COF and wear rate, or lack evidence of a denser composite oxide layer compared to the control films, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractAlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy (HEA) films with strong amorphization were obtained by co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition, and the effect of thermal shock on the films was investigated in order to explore the protection mechanism of HEA films against mechanical components in extreme service environments. The results show that after annealing at 800 °C for 1 h, the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the surface actively prevents the oxidation from continuing, so that the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film exhibits excellent oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air. In the friction-corrosion coupling environment, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film annealed at 800 °C for 1 h shows the best tribocorrosion resistance due to the stable dense microstructure and excellent mechanical properties, and its ΔOCP, COF and wear rate possess the smallest values of 0.055, 0.04 and 1.34 × 10−6 mm−3·N−1·m−1.Keywords: AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film, thermal shock, oxidation, tribocorrosion

Filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (FCVAD) has sufficient advantages to obtain multi-component films due to its characteristics of magnetic filtration, high ionization rate (100%) and controllable ion types and ion energy. Co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (Co-FCVAD) is obtained by designing a multi-channel for particle transport based on FCVAD, which significantly improves the defects of uncontrollable composition and poor quality in the preparation of HEA films [,]. Thus, in order to improve the performance of mechanical components in extreme service environments, the AlCrTiZrMo film system is determined by selecting elements with a large atomic radius difference and excellent corrosion and high temperature performance. In this work, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film is prepared based on Co-FCVAD. The synergistic interaction between elements at a high temperature in air is discussed, and the changes in microstructure, mechanical properties and tribocorrosion properties of the film after annealing at different temperatures are studied, so as to analyze the protection mechanisms of AlCrTiZrMo HEA films in the simulated scenario of thermal shock.
